Two phones, three paths
How V-Pad reaches your computer depends on your phone — and on whether you want to install anything over there. This is the one thing worth knowing before you start.
The phone presents itself as a real Bluetooth gamepad and pairs with your PC or console directly. Nothing to install on the computer — no driver, no helper. Pair it like any controller and play.

The same gamepad, carried over your own Wi-Fi instead. This is the path when your PC has no Bluetooth — or when you want more than one phone in the game, up to four at once. It asks for two free installs on Windows, once: the ViGEmBus driver, then V-Pad Helper.
Downloads and steps

Apple reserves the Bluetooth gamepad role for the system, so no iPhone app can appear in your computer's Bluetooth list. Wi-Fi is the only path: a small free helper runs on your PC, and the two find each other on your own network.
The iPhone helper

What is the driver for? Over Bluetooth, Windows already has the driver it needs built in. Over Wi-Fi your presses arrive as network traffic, so something has to present a controller to Windows — that is the only thing ViGEmBus does. It is made and signed by its own author, and installed once.

Why not Bluetooth on iPhone? A platform restriction, not a missing feature: iOS refuses to let third-party apps advertise the Bluetooth HID service. Every iPhone app in this category ships a desktop companion for the same reason.

Install the ViGEmBus driver — download, install and forget

This is what lets a game believe a real controller is plugged in: your presses arrive as network traffic, so something has to present a controller to Windows — that is the only thing this driver does. It is made and signed by its own author, so Windows will not complain. Download it, double-click, answer Yes, then Next → Install → Finish. You only ever do this once: ViGEmBus is built to sit in the background — install it and leave it. You never run it, never install it again and never update it.

Download V-Pad Helper — run it when you want to play games

Double-click vpad-host.exe. Windows shows a blue warning the first time because the file is not signed yet — choose More info, then Run anyway. No black console window appears; instead you get a window with a QR code and a 6-digit number. Leave it open, your phone needs it in a moment. A small V-Pad icon also appears by the clock, bottom-right — that is the helper, and it keeps running after you close the window. It has to stay running while you play.

Current build 1.0.3 (e0e3dd9), 17 September 2026. For the best experience keep an eye on updates: when a new host is out, V-Pad's changelog in the app tells you — download the new vpad-host.exe then and run it while you play.

Phone and computer on the same Wi-Fi. Open V-Pad, choose Wi-Fi, and either scan that QR code or type the six digits. Please include: your phone model and OS version, whether the computer is Windows or macOS, and — if the helper is involved — the log file (its tray menu has Open log folder). The log says exactly which step failed and saves a lot of back and forth.
Troubleshooting
The phone doesn't find my computer

Both must be on the same Wi-Fi network. The single most common cause is a VPN running on the computer: it hands out an address on a different network than the phone's. The helper's tray menu lists the addresses it published — the phone must be on one of those. Guest and corporate networks often block the discovery protocol (mDNS) entirely; a normal home network does not.
It's listed but connecting fails
The Windows firewall prompt was most likely declined. Open Windows Defender Firewall → Allow an app through firewall and tick V-Pad Helper for private networks. Then quit and reopen the helper.
Connected, but the game sees no controller

Windows: the gamepad driver (ViGEmBus) is missing. The helper offers it on first run; you can also install it any time from the tray menu, and it says so plainly when it is absent. After installing, check Win+R → joy.cpl: an "Xbox 360 Controller for Windows" should be listed. If the driver was just installed, quit and reopen the helper. In Steam, also enable Settings → Controller → Generic Gamepad Configuration Support.

macOS: grant Accessibility permission to the helper (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility), otherwise macOS accepts the input and silently discards it. Note that on macOS the pad is mapped to keyboard and mouse, not to a real controller — games that require a gamepad will not see one.
Windows says the file isn't safe

The helper is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC" for any new file it has not seen before. Choose More info → Run anyway. The source is public if you want to check it first.
I ran the helper and no window opened
That is normal — it is a tray app, not a window. Look next to the clock; on Windows 11 new tray icons start out hidden behind the ^ arrow. A notification on first run confirms it started.
